title: Jesu, the Life, the Truth, the Way
description: Jesu, the Life, the Truth, the Way in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 357. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-su, the Life, the Truth, the Way, In whom I now be-lieve, As taught by thee, in faith I pray, Ex-pect-ing to re-ceive.

lines: Jesu, the Life, the Truth, the Way,
In whom I now believe,
As taught by thee, in faith I pray,
Expecting to receive.
Thy will by me on earth be done,
As by the choirs above,
Who always see thee on thy throne,
And glory in thy love.
I ask in confidence the grace,
That I may do thy will,
As angels, who behold thy face,
And all thy words fulfil.
Surely I shall, the sinner I
Shall serve thee without fear;
My heart no longer gives the lie
To my deceitful prayer.
When thou the work of faith hast wrought,
I shall be pure within,
Nor sin in deed, or word, or thought;
For angels never sin.
From thee no more shall I depart,
No more unfaithful prove,
But love thee with a constant heart;
For angels always love.
I all thy holy will shall prove:
I, a weak, sinful worm,
When thee with all my heart I love,
Shall all thy law perform.
The graces of my second birth
To me shall all be given;
And I shall do thy will on earth,
As angels do in heaven.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
